length.text: Long and slender; the longest museum specimen was 168 cm

reproduction.text: Lays eggs, 4 to 13 at a time

overview.text: The Savanna Vine Snake, or Twig Snake, is a very thin, long-tailed tree snake of southern Africa. It is dangerously venomous even though its fangs are at the back of the mouth.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Slender with a long tail. The longest museum specimen, a male, measured 168 cm, of which 62 cm was tail.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: South-eastern Africa: north-eastern South Africa, Eswatini, southern Mozambique and Malawi.

behaviour.text: Active by day and spends much of its time climbing in bushes and trees.

behaviour.label: Bites
behaviour.text: Its venom is delivered by large grooved teeth at the back of the upper jaw. The German snake scientist Robert Mertens died after being bitten by one.

reproduction.text: Lays 4 to 13 small, long eggs, each about 36 mm long and 16 mm wide.

funfacts.text: Its thin body and twig-like colours let it vanish among branches.
